F01.name: Controlled Fire
F01.fx: +1 Production in all cities (work by firelight); +1 Food from Tundra tiles in all cities (warmth). The foundation: fire makes every settlement a little more productive and the cold lands habitable.
F01.conj: The fire that lightning leaves might be fed, carried home and kept alive.

F02.name: Kiln Construction
F02.fx: Shrine (and the Maya Pyramid it is replaced by). +25% City Strength from defensive buildings — walls of fired brick. Kiln heat — fired pots, glazes, fired brick — leads on to Glassmaking and Geopolymer Concrete.

F03.name: Charcoal Production
F03.fx: +25% Production when constructing Melee units in all cities — hotter fires, harder blades. The hotter fire that makes smelting and iron possible. Wood tar, the kiln's by-product: -25% maintenance on road & railroads; +10% Strength <for Water units> — tarred roads, caulked hulls.

F04.name: Smelting Discovery
F04.fx: Unlocks Metallurgy focus. +1 Production from Copper tiles in all cities and +1 Gold from Gold Ore tiles in all cities — the ores Ore Identification revealed become worth working.
F04.flav: The moment someone put green rock near hot charcoal.

F05.name: Signal Fires
F05.fx: Signal Fire [improvement on Hill; 5 turns; +1 Sight; Gives a defensive bonus of 20%]. An early-warning post on high ground.

F06.name: Greek Fire
F06.prereq: F03 (Charcoal Production — wood tar) + O08 (Geological Observation — sulphur)
F06.fx: Fire Ship [unit, Melee Water; cost 70; mv 4; str 14; +50% Strength <when attacking>; +50% Strength <vs Water units>]; +25% Strength <for Siege units> <vs cities> <when attacking>. Pine pitch, sulfur and a siphon — no petroleum required. Also discoverable through Warfare or Seafaring focus.

F07.name: Advanced Pyrotechnics
F07.prereq: F03 + O08 (Geological Observation — sulphur) + MI08 (Saltpeter Mining — the oxidiser)
F07.fx: Fireworks Ground 70/1; +1 Culture, +1 Happiness; requires Saltpeter. Prerequisite for Gunpowder unless GUNPOWDER_ABSENT.

F09.name: Controlled Burn Agriculture
F09.fx: -50% construction time for Remove Forest improvements and -50% construction time for Remove Jungle improvements; +25% Yield from pillaging tiles (burning what you clear). Land is opened fast — and what is burnt gives back.

F10.name: Thermal Lance
F10.fx: +30% Production when constructing All wonders in all cities. Stone shaped by directed heat.
F10.flav: Speculative: what if directed-heat tools were developed early?

F11.name: Volcanic Forge Tradition
F11.fx: Volcanic Forge [replaces Forge; 120/1; +2 Production; +1 Production from Volcanic tiles in this city; +15% Production when constructing Land units in this city; Must have an owned Volcanic within 2 tiles]. Civ unique: +1 Production from Volcanic tiles in all cities — the more vents you hold, the more you forge.
F11.flav: Icelandic/Japanese tradition of forging with Earth's own heat.

F15.name: Signal Fire Network
F15.prereq: F05 (Signal Fires) + WA06 (Fortification Design) + Mountain/highland or Many neighbors biome
F15.fx: Signal Tower [20/0; +10% Strength for cities (applies to this city)]. Civ unique: +20% Strength <for Military units> <when defending> <in Hill tiles> — the high ground warns and holds.
F15.flav: Greek phryctoriae, Chinese beacon towers, Gondor. Relocated from the former Communications focus.

F16.name: Turbary
F16.fx: Peat Cutting (improvement; terrainsCanBeBuiltOn: Marsh; 6 turns; +2 Production; Does not need removal of Marsh) — fuel burned where it lies. A bog can now be drained (the Aqueduct's flood control, WM02) or cut. A worked Peat Cutting also counts as a fuel tile for a Charcoal Kiln, and lets a city's Distillery make Whisky. Needs a Marsh in the civilisation's territory: a people with no bogs never learns to burn them.
F16.flav: Pliny described the Chauci burning peat in the first century AD.

G01.name: Plant Identification
G01.fx: Forager's Hut 10/0; +1 Food. Edible plants and simple remedies; the first building of every camp.
G01.conj: Some plants feed us and some sicken us; there may be a way to tell them apart.

G02.name: Seed Saving
G02.flav: The moment someone realised that seeds could be planted deliberately.

G03.name: Herbal Medicine
G03.fx: Herbalist [10/0; Military Units adjacent to this city heal +5 HP per turn when healing].

G04.name: Fermentation
G04.fx: +1 Gold from Wine tiles in all cities — fermentation makes the grape a trade good. Beer may have driven civilisation.

G05.name: Insect Cultivation
G05.fx: +1 Gold from Silk tiles in all cities — sericulture. Protein on any terrain. Prerequisite for Silk Production.

G06.name: Mycological Knowledge
G06.fx: Mushroom Cellar [30/0; +1 Food from Forest tiles in this city; +1 Food from Jungle tiles in this city — mushrooms from woods left standing].
G06.conj: The moulds that spoil our bread may have uses we have not yet guessed.

G07.name: Botanical Classification
G07.fx: Garden; Plantation (improvement); +10% Insight to Farming and Medicine.

G08.name: Three Sisters Agriculture
G08.prereq: G02 + Temperate or Tropical biome + River or Wetland terrain
G08.fx: Three Sisters Plot [replaces Granary; 60/1; +2 Food; +1 Food from Wheat tiles in this city; +1 Food from Bananas tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Food from {River} {Grassland} tiles in all cities — companion planting on fertile river land.
G08.flav: Haudenosaunee-inspired. Complementary crop sets arise naturally in warm, fertile regions.

G09.name: Permaculture Principles
G09.fx: Food Forest [improvement on Forest or Jungle; 10 turns; +2 Food; Does not need removal of Forest; Does not need removal of Jungle]. Food forever, without felling.

G10.name: Psychoactive Plant Knowledge
G10.fx: +1 Faith from Incense tiles in all cities — resins burned for visions. Ceremony as inquiry.
G10.conj: Certain resins and leaves bring visions; our priests might learn their use.

G11.name: Jungle Canopy Living
G11.fx: Canopy Market [replaces Market; 100/0; +2 Gold; Gold +25%; Merchant ×1; +1 Gold from Jungle tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Food from Jungle tiles in all cities — every jungle tile feeds you, so felling one costs you.

G12.name: Dreamtime Pathways
G12.fx: Songline Waystation [20/0; +1 Gold from each Trade Route; +1 Culture from Desert tiles in this city]. Civ uniques: all Land units gain the Songline promotion (Double movement in Desert; +1 Sight), and +1 Culture from Desert tiles in all cities. The featureless land is a map you carry in your head.

G13.name: Sacred Grove Tradition
G13.fx: Sacred Grove [improvement on Forest; 6 turns; +1 Faith, +1 Culture; Does not need removal of Forest; Irremovable — the grove cannot be chopped]. Civ unique: +1 Faith from Forest tiles without Improvement in all cities — the uncut forest is itself a temple.

S01.name: Tool Knapping
S01.fx: Warrior, Scout (units); Remove Forest, Remove Jungle (improvements). Stone tools: the first weapons and the first clearing of land.
S01.conj: A stone struck at the right angle might split into an edge sharper than any tooth.

S02.name: Grinding & Polishing
S02.fx: -25% construction time for Quarry improvements — polished stone cuts stone. Polished tools and decorative stonework.
S02.flav: The Neolithic revolution in tool quality.

S03.name: Quarrying
S03.fx: Walls, Stone Works (and the Babylonian Walls of Babylon); Quarry (improvement); unlocks Construction focus.

S04.name: Ore Identification
S04.fx: Reveals Copper, Gold Ore, Gems and Iron (their revealedBy — hidden until now); Mine (improvement); unlocks Mining focus. Suddenly you see where the wealth is buried.
S04.flav: Suddenly you see where the wealth is buried.

S05.name: Obsidian Working
S05.fx: Reveals Obsidian (new luxury resource, found on Volcanic tiles; improved by Mine); Obsidian Warrior unit, Sword type; cost 45; mv 2; str 10; requires Obsidian. Sharper than steel, and a luxury besides.
S05.conj: Volcanic glass might flake to an edge keener than any blade we can forge.

S07.name: Flint Knapping Mastery
S07.fx: +10% Strength <for Ranged units>. Better points fly truer.
S07.conj: Flint shaped with patience might give our arrows truer, keener points.

S08.name: Jade/Gemstone Working
S08.fx: Jeweler [95/1; +2 Gold; +1 Gold from Gems tiles in this city; +1 Gold from Silver tiles in this city; Provides 1 Jewelry].

S09.name: Geopolymer Concrete
S09.fx: Geopolymer Works [30/0; cityHealth +25; -25% maintenance cost for All buildings in this city]. Buildings that shrug off siege and time — without the Roman Concrete path.

S10.name: Obsidian Trade Empire
S10.fx: Obsidian Exchange [replaces Market; 100/0; +3 Gold; Gold +25%; Merchant ×1; +2 Gold from Obsidian tiles in this city]. Civ uniques: +2 Gold from Volcanic tiles in all cities; +1 Production from Obsidian tiles in all cities. Every vent you hold is a trade good.
S10.flav: Mesoamerican obsidian trade networks spanned thousands of miles.

S11.name: Megalithic Observatory
S11.prereq: CU02 (Monumental Architecture — the megaliths) + O01 + Isolated start or Coastal start
S11.fx: Standing Stones national wonder; 100/0; +3 Science, +2 Faith; +10% Insight to Observation and Mathematics. Civ unique: +1 Science from all World Wonder buildings and +1 Science from all Monument buildings — every monument is an instrument.

O01.name: Star Tracking
O01.fx: +1 Movement <for Scout units> (navigating by the stars).
O01.conj: The stars rise in the same order every night; they might mark the seasons and the way home.

O02.name: Weather Prediction
O02.fx: +5% growth in all cities and +1 Sight <for Water units> — reading the sky for the field and the sea.

O03.name: Animal Behavior Study
O03.fx: Unlocks Animal Husbandry focus; Camp (improvement — hunting grounds; moved here from O09).
O03.conj: The herds come to the same water at the same hour; their ways might be learned.

O04.name: Tidal Patterns
O04.fx: Tidal Weir [10/0; +1 Food from Fish tiles in this city; Must be next to Coast].

O05.name: Celestial Mathematics
O05.fx: Unlocks Mathematics focus; +2 Faith in capital (foretold eclipses).

O06.name: Natural Philosophy
O06.fx: The Oracle (world wonder); National College (national wonder — the Academy); +5% Insight to all foci.

O08.name: Geological Observation
O08.fx: Reveal up to all Strategic resource within a 10 tile radius (a Triggerable map reveal on discovery — the deposits Ore Identification missed); +1 Production from Quarry tiles in all cities; +1 Production from Iron tiles in all cities (magnetic ore sorting); +1 Culture in capital — the lodestone, a geological curiosity. Prerequisite for the Compass. +1 Gold from all Dye Works buildings (bleaching); +1 Happiness in capital (antiseptic, and matches that strike anywhere) — sulphur

O09.name: Migratory Pattern Mapping
O09.fx: Circus; +1 Food from Camp tiles in all cities — knowing where the herds will be.
O09.conj: If we knew where the herds go each season, we could be waiting for them.

O10.name: Antikythera-Style Mechanism
O10.fx: Antikythera Engine [national wonder; 120/0; +3 Science, +2 Culture; +15% Science in this city]; +15% Insight to Mathematics and Observation. Seed of the Antikythera chain (O13/O14/O15).
O10.flav: What if the Antikythera tradition continued?

O13.name: Mechanical Ephemeris
O13.fx: +1 Movement <for Water units> (perfect celestial navigation); Ephemeris House [25/0; +1 Gold from each Trade Route — navigational data sold to all comers].
O13.flav: Extending the Antikythera tradition into practical navigation.

O14.name: Tide Computing Engine
O14.fx: Tide Computer [105/1; requires a Harbor in this city; +1 Production, +1 Gold from Water resource tiles in this city; Must be next to Coast; +100% Production when constructing Seaport buildings in this city] — a Seaport a century early, and so, like the Engine House, an early version that converts: the ruleset derivation gives the canonical Seaport Remove Tide Computer in this city, so a Seaport goes up twice as fast where a Tide Computer stands and absorbs it, rather than dou
O14.flav: Lord Kelvin built one in 1873 — what if it came centuries earlier?

O15.name: Mechanical Weather Predictor
O15.fx: Weather Station [250/2; +10% growth in this city; +1 Food from Farm tiles in this city]. Also discoverable through Mechanics.
O15.flav: The ultimate expression of the Antikythera tradition — mechanical computers applied to nature.

O16.name: Sacred Astronomy Tradition
O16.fx: Mountain Observatory [40/1; +2 Science, +1 Faith; Must be next to Mountain — an Observatory available from the Primitive era]. Civ unique: +1 Science from Hill tiles in all cities — the high country watches the sky.

SO01.name: Basic Counting
SO01.fx: +25% Gold from Trade Routes (bookkeeping makes city connections pay); the yield display shows exact figures (UI).
SO01.conj: Notches cut in a stick might keep track of days, of stores and of people.

SO02.name: Storytelling
SO02.fx: Monument (and the Ethiopian Stele). Culture generation begins.
SO02.conj: The elders’ tales might keep what they learned alive after they are gone.

SO03.name: Tribal Law
SO03.fx: +1 Happiness in capital; +1 Unit Supply per city — a settled people can field and feed a warband. Prerequisite for Formation Fighting.

SO04.name: Writing
SO04.fx: Library; The Great Library (world wonder); Enables establishment of embassies (the canonical Writing unique); unlocks Trade focus. Transformative.

SO05.name: Specialization of Labor
SO05.fx: +1 Production from every specialist in all cities. Also switches the research routing from 50/50 to 80/20 (Section 1.2) — a society that has specialised its labour can direct its inquiry.

SO06.name: Codified Law
SO06.fx: Courthouse. Codified law lets annexed cities be governed.

SO08.name: Census
SO08.fx: +1 Gold per 4 population in all cities — knowing how many there are to tax.

SO09.name: Quipu/Non-Written Recording
SO09.fx: Quipu Archive [replaces Library; 75/1; +1 Science per 2 population in this city; +1 Gold from each Trade Route]. Civ unique: +25% Gold from Trade Routes. Unlocks Trade focus (the alternative to Writing for this purpose).

SO10.name: Guilds
SO10.fx: Machu Picchu (world wonder); Guild Hall [70/1; Merchant ×1; +1 Production from every specialist in this city]; Enables conversion of city production to Gold (the canonical Guilds unique).

SO11.name: Banking
SO11.fx: Bank (and the Persian Satrap's Court), Coffee House; Forbidden Palace (world wonder); unlocks Economics-tier trade breakthroughs. National Treasury (national wonder) — every debit matched by a credit: the Medici kept double-entry books.

SO13.name: Meritocratic Civil Service
SO13.fx: Chichen Itza (world wonder); Examination Hall [50/1; +1 Production from every specialist in this city; -15% maintenance cost for All buildings in this city].

SO14.name: Oral Epic Tradition
SO14.prereq: SO02 + CU03 (Artistic Tradition) + no SO04 (Writing) yet
SO14.fx: Bard Council replaces Amphitheater; 100/2; requires a Monument in this city; +3 Culture, +1 Happiness; Artist ×1; Great Artist points 3. Civ unique: +1 Culture per 2 social policies adopted — the Epic grows a verse with every turn of your culture.

SO16.name: Public Education
SO16.fx: Public School — CORE because Unciv's Research Lab requires it. Constabulary and Police Station (both <when espionage is enabled>) — the state that polices its own territory; +2 Unit Supply per city — the nation in arms, fed from cans: Napoleon offered the prize that Appert won in 1810. The nineteenth-century state schooled and conscripted together.
SO16.flav: Prussia made schooling compulsory in 1763, and other states followed.

FA01.name: Irrigation
FA01.fx: Unlocks Water Management focus. +1 Food from {Farm} {Fresh Water} tiles in all cities — the canonical Civil-Service farm bonus, arriving with the first irrigation ditch. (Farms already build on Hills in Civ V.)

FA02.name: Crop Rotation
FA02.fx: +1 Food from Wheat tiles in all cities — the soil no longer tires.

FA03.name: Selective Breeding
FA03.prereq: G02 + AH02 + (G07 or (FA01 + FA02)) — Seed Saving and Herd Animal Domestication; then Botanical Classification, or Irrigation with Crop Rotation
FA03.fx: +1 Food from Plantation tiles in all cities — improved varieties of every cultivated crop. +1 Production from Pasture tiles in all cities (wool, hide, horn); War Dog [unit, Melee; cost 35; mv 3; str 7; Also discoverable through Animal Husbandry.
FA03.flav: Improved varieties of every cultivated crop.

FA06.name: Nitrogen Fixation Awareness
FA06.fx: +1 Food from Farm tiles without Fresh Water in all cities — legumes rescue the dry farms that irrigation could not reach.

FA07.name: Chinampa (Floating Gardens)
FA07.fx: Chinampa Garden [replaces Water Mill; 75/2; +2 Food, +1 Production; +1 Food from Lakes tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Food from Lakes tiles in all cities — every lake is a field. (The Aztec Floating Gardens remain Aztec.)

FA09.name: Greenhouse Cultivation
FA09.fx: Greenhouse [70/1; +1 Food from Tundra tiles in this city; +1 Food from Snow tiles in this city; +1 Food from Desert tiles in this city]. Any crop in any climate — under glass.

FA10.name: Hydroponics
FA10.fx: Hydroponics Lab [375/2; +2 Food; -10% Food consumption by Population in this city]. Food without soil.

FA11.name: Vertical Farming
FA11.prereq: FA10 + CO11 (Reinforced Concrete) + EN06 (Semiconductor Mastery — LED grow lights)
FA11.fx: +1 Gold from all Hydroponics Lab buildings — produce grown and sold inside the city.

FA13.name: Flood Harvest Tradition
FA13.fx: Nilometer [65/1; +2 Food, +1 Culture; +1 Food from Flood plains tiles in this city; Must be on River]. Civ unique: +1 Food, +1 Production from Flood plains tiles in all cities — the inundation is a gift, and you have learned to read it.

FA14.name: Pastoral Nomadism
FA14.prereq: G02 + AH02 + Grassland/steppe biome + low city count (≤2)
FA14.fx: Yurt Camp 40/1; +1 Food, +1 Production, +1 Culture. Civ uniques: +1 Food from Grassland tiles without Improvement in all cities (the herds feed on open range — improving the grass ends it) and +1 Movement <for Settler units>. Few cities, wide range.

FA15.name: Mountain Terrace Farming
FA15.fx: Terrace Granary [replaces Granary; 60/1; +2 Food; +1 Production from Hill tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Food from Hill tiles in all cities — the slopes are carved into fields. (The Inca Terrace farm remains Inca.)
FA15.flav: Incan andenes, Philippine Banaue, Balinese subak.

FA16.name: Nitrate Fertiliser
FA16.fx: +1 Food from Farm tiles in all cities <when number of Saltpeter is more than 0> <before discovering Catalysis> — mined nitrates and guano on every field, for as long as you hold Saltpeter: the Haber process's bonus, bought with a resource the musket also wants. The bonus simply passes to the Haber process, which needs no Saltpeter.
FA16.flav: Before 1913 the world's fields were fed from Chilean nitrate and Peruvian guano.

AH01.name: Dog Domestication
AH01.fx: +1 Sight <for Scout units>; +1 Food from Deer tiles in all cities. The first companion, and the first hunting partner.
AH01.flav: The first animal people ever domesticated.

AH02.name: Herd Animal Domestication
AH02.fx: Pasture (improvement). Prerequisite for Weaving — wool and leather.

AH03.name: Horse Domestication
AH03.fx: Reveals Horses (their revealedBy); Stable; Circus Maximus (national wonder); +1 Production from Horses tiles in all cities.

AH05.name: Camel Domestication
AH05.fx: Civilian units gain the Camel Train promotion (Double movement in Desert); No Maintenance costs for improvements in Desert tiles. The desert becomes a road.
AH05.conj: The desert beast that stores its water might carry our goods.

AH06.name: Elephant Domestication
AH06.fx: Elephant Cavalry [unit, Mounted; cost 70; mv 3; str 12; +25% Strength <vs Mounted units>; No defensive terrain bonus; requires Ivory]; +1 Production from Ivory tiles in all cities (elephants haul stone). (India's War Elephant remains Indian.)
AH06.conj: The great beasts of the forest might be tamed to haul and to carry.

AH07.name: Falconry
AH07.fx: +1 Sight <for Ranged units>; New Ranged units start with 15 XP in all cities — archers trained beside the hawk.

AH08.name: Carrier Pigeon Networks
AH08.fx: Pigeon Loft [70/1; +1 Gold from each Trade Route; +25% spy effectiveness in this city (<when espionage is enabled>)].

AH10.name: Llama/Alpaca Domestication
AH10.fx: Llama Pen [30/1; +1 Food, +1 Production; +1 Production from Sheep tiles in this city]. Civ uniques: No Maintenance costs for improvements in Hill tiles, and Land units gain the Llama Train promotion (Double movement in Hill). Pack animals without horses, on the roof of the world.

AH11.name: Veterinary Medicine
AH11.fx: Veterinary College [40/0; Mounted Units adjacent to this city heal +10 HP per turn when healing; +1 Food from Cattle tiles in this city].

AH12.name: Reindeer Herding
AH12.fx: Reindeer Sled [unit, Scout type; cost 30; mv 4; str 5; Double movement in Tundra; Double movement in Snow]; Herder Camp [20/0; +1 Food; +1 Food from Tundra tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Production from Tundra tiles in all cities — the herd is transport, food, leather and trade.

AH13.name: Steppe Rider Tradition
AH13.fx: Horse Archer unit, Mounted; cost 60; mv 4; str 6; ranged str 9; range 2; Can move after attacking; No defensive terrain bonus; requires Horses — available without Composite Bow; Nomad Camp [replaces Barracks; 75/1; +1 Production; New Mounted units start with 15 XP in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Movement <for Mounted units> — born in the saddle.

AH14.name: War Elephant Tradition
AH14.fx: Armoured Elephant [unit, Mounted; cost 100; mv 3; str 18; +25% Strength <when attacking>; No defensive terrain bonus; requires Ivory]; Elephant Stable [replaces Stable; 100/1; +15% Production when constructing Mounted units in this city; +1 Production from Ivory tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Production from Jungle tiles in all cities — the forest that feeds the herds.

MI05.name: Deep Shaft Mining
MI05.fx: Reveals Silver and Salt (deep deposits — the second reveal); +1 Production from Mine tiles in all cities. Going underground changes everything.

MI06.name: Coal Discovery
MI06.fx: Reveals Coal (the canonical Industrialization revealedBy); +1 Production from Coal tiles in all cities. Absent in FOSSIL_FUELS_ABSENT worlds, where there is no coal to discover: the Removal Truth gives Coal Doesn't generate naturally, and a discovery with nothing to find does not exist. Charcoal and renewable paths substitute.
MI06.flav: The fuel of the industrial revolution.

MI06B.name: Volcanic Ash Processing
MI06B.fx: Pozzolana Works [20/0; cityHealth +10; -25% maintenance cost for All buildings in this city; Must have an owned Volcanic within 2 tiles]; +1 Food from Volcanic tiles in all cities (fertile ash). Prerequisite for Roman Concrete.
MI06B.flav: Fertile ash for the fields, and a binding powder for the builders.

MI07.name: Petroleum Discovery
MI07.prereq: MI05 + O08 (Geological Observation) + MC08 (Steam Engine — the steam-driven drilling rig, and an industry that wanted lamp oil)
MI07.fx: Reveals Oil (the canonical Biology revealedBy); Oil well, Offshore Platform (improvements); +1 Gold from Oil tiles in all cities (kerosene). Absent in FOSSIL_FUELS_ABSENT worlds, where there is no petroleum to discover: the Removal Truth gives Oil Doesn't generate naturally, and a discovery with nothing to find does not exist. Bio-organic chemistry and alcohol engines substitute.
MI07.flav: Kerosene for the lamps, before any engine wanted the oil.

MI08.name: Saltpeter Mining
MI08.prereq: MI05 + CH01 (Alchemy — saltpetre was an alchemist's find)
MI08.fx: Reveals Saltpeter (new strategic resource; on Desert, Plains and Hill tiles; improved by Mine; deposits of 2–4, like Iron); +1 Unit Supply per city (preserved rations). The gunpowder strategic — consumed by the Musketman, the Cannon and the Fireworks Ground; the Air Rifleman pointedly needs none. A civilisation in a gunpowder world without nitre fights with pikes and crossbows until Rifling, exactly as an iron-less civilisation fights with Pikemen — and trades or marches for
MI08.flav: Nitre for the army: preserved rations, and gunpowder.

MI11.name: Rare Earth Extraction
MI11.fx: Reveals Rare Earths (new strategic resource; on Hills and Mountain-adjacent tiles; improved by Mine; each deposit provides 2–4, like Aluminum); +1 Science from Rare Earths tiles in all cities. The late-game high-tech strategic Civ V never had: consumed by the Microchip Foundry, the Fab, the Drone and the Solar Farm, and a prerequisite for Miniaturisation. A civilisation without it cannot build the electronics line — or must trade, conquer, or (Substance worlds) transmute for
MI11.conj: Rare metals hidden in dull-looking ores might be separated out, one by one.

MI12.name: Asteroid Prospecting
MI12.fx: Asteroid Mining Station [940/5; Provides 2 Iron; Provides 2 Aluminum; Provides 2 Aluminum <after discovering Orbital Resource Delivery>; Provides 2 Rare Earths <after discovering Orbital Resource Delivery>; Limited to 3 per Civilization] — the Recycling Center pattern: strategic resources from orbit end scarcity.

MI13.name: Wood Gas Production
MI13.fx: -25% construction time for Lumber mill improvements — timber becomes fuel. Strategically critical in FOSSIL_FUELS_ABSENT worlds. Also discoverable through Chemistry.
MI13.flav: Wood-gas lorries were common in fuel-starved Europe in the Second World War.

MI14.name: Deep Earth Tradition
MI14.fx: Mining Temple [replaces Stone Works; 75/1; +1 Production, +1 Faith; +1 Production from Mine tiles in this city; +5% Insight to Mining]. Civ unique: +1 Production from {Mine} {Hill} tiles in all cities — the mountain's mines are sacred, and they pay.
MI14.flav: Cornish/Saxon/Andean mining traditions where mining was a sacred craft.

ME01.name: Copper Working
ME01.fx: Copper Warrior unit, Melee; cost 45; mv 2; str 9 (Warrior 8); requires Copper. The first worked metal, in the first metal hand.
ME01.flav: The first worked metal, in the first metal hand.

ME-B.name: Bellows
ME-B.fx: Forge (the canonical Metal Casting building: +15% Production when constructing Land units in this city, +1 Production from Iron tiles in this city). Forced air makes the iron path possible.
ME-B.flav: Forced air changes everything about metallurgy.

ME02.name: Bronze Alloy
ME02.prereq: ME01 + Copper in territory (extracted, traded or captured)
ME02.fx: Statue of Zeus (world wonder); +10% Strength <for Melee units> (bronze arms and armour). Requires Copper in territory (Civ V has no tin; the resource rule of Section 1.2 applies).

ME04.name: Iron Smelting
ME04.prereq: F03 (Charcoal) + ME-B (Bellows) + iron deposits in territory
ME04.fx: Swordsman (unit); Colossus (world wonder). The Iron Age begins.

ME05.name: Steel Production
ME05.fx: Pikeman (unit); +1 Gold from Iron tiles in all cities — pots, pans and pipes. (The Longswordsman and Armory move to Plate Armour, ME18; the Arsenal and Kremlin to Star Fort, CO25; the Knight to Stirrup, WA27.)
ME05.flav: China cast iron and made steel from it in the same centuries.

ME06.name: Damascus/Wootz Steel
ME06.prereq: ME05 (Steel) + MI05 (Deep Mining) + Desert/arid or Tropical biome
ME06.fx: Swordsmith [replaces Armory; 160/1; requires a Barracks in this city; New Military units start with 15 XP in this city; +2 Gold from each Trade Route — blades sold across the world]. Civ unique: +10% Strength <for Melee units>.
ME06.flav: Indian/Middle Eastern technique — requires specific high-carbon ore deposits found in warm climates.

ME08.name: Blast Furnace
ME08.prereq: ME04 + CO02 (Post and Lintel) + (WM05 or MC04 — bellows driven by a mill) + (MI06 or F03) — Coal Discovery, or Charcoal Production
ME08.fx: Ironworks (national wonder). Requires Coal. Charcoal Kiln [210/2; Provides 1 Coal <in cities without a Distillery> <when number of [Worked [non-[{non-Forest} {non-Jungle} {non-Peat Cutting}]] Tiles in this city] is more than 2> and Provides 1 Coal <in cities with a Distillery> <when number of [[Worked [non-[{non-Forest} {non-Jungle} {non-Peat Cutting}]] Tiles in this city] - min([Worked Peat Cutting Tiles in this city], 1)] is more than 2>; -10% Production in this city <in ci
ME08.flav: Sweden ran charcoal blast furnaces into the 19th century.

ME09.name: Crucible Steel
ME09.fx: +10% Strength <for Melee units> — the finest pre-industrial steel. (Stacks with a Damascus tradition, as it did historically.)

ME12.name: Bessemer Process
ME12.fx: Battleship (unit — steel hulls); +1 Production from Iron tiles in all cities (cheap steel). Prerequisite for Railway Network and Reinforced Concrete.
ME12.flav: Cheap steel: steel hulls and steel rails.

ME13.name: Aluminium Extraction
ME13.fx: Reveals Aluminum (the canonical Electricity revealedBy); +1 Production from Aluminum tiles in all cities.

ME15.name: Memory Alloys
ME15.fx: -33% maintenance cost for All buildings in all cities (structures that repair themselves); all Military units gain the Adaptive Armour promotion (+10% Strength <when defending>).

ME16.name: Sacred Bronze Tradition
ME16.fx: Bronze Foundry Temple [replaces Temple; 100/2; requires a Shrine in this city; +2 Faith, +1 Production, +1 Culture; Provides 1 Copper — the base luxury, cast rather than mined]. Civ unique: +1 Culture, +1 Faith from Copper tiles in all cities — the metal is sacred before it is useful.
ME16.flav: Shang/Zhou Chinese ritual bronzes, West African Benin bronzes.

ME17.name: Assaying
ME17.fx: Mint — metal tested for its purity, so the coin can be trusted.

ME18.name: Plate Armour
ME18.prereq: ME05 (Steel) + (WM05 or MC04 — a mill to drive the hammers)
ME18.fx: Longswordsman (unit); Armory — steel beaten to shape under mill-driven hammers.
ME18.flav: Steel beaten to shape under water-driven hammers, 14th–15th century.

CO01.name: Mud Brick Construction
CO01.fx: Granary. Sun-dried brick bound with the straw of the first harvests: the first permanent architecture.
CO01.flav: Sun-dried brick bound with the straw of the first harvests.

CO02.name: Post and Lintel
CO02.fx: Colosseum; Lumber mill (improvement); the Polynesian Moai.

CO03.name: Arch Construction
CO03.fx: Road; Roads connect tiles across rivers (the canonical Engineering unique — bridges); +5% Production when constructing All buildings in all cities (the arch spans wider rooms). Prerequisite for the Aqueduct. Post Office [55/1; +1 Gold; +1 Gold from each Trade Route; +25% spy effectiveness in this city (<when espionage is enabled>)] — the post rides the roads: the Persian royal road, the Roman cursus publicus.
CO03.flav: The arch spans wider rooms, and carries the road across the river.

CO04.name: Roman Concrete
CO04.fx: Concrete Works [40/0; cityHealth +25; -10% maintenance cost for All buildings in this city — seawater-proof harbours]. Lost for a millennium, in our world.
CO04.flav: Seawater-proof harbours, from a recipe later lost for a millennium.

CO05.name: Corbel Arch/Vault
CO05.fx: Corbel Vault [30/0; cityStrength +3; 10% Food is carried over after population increases in this city — cool undercrofts]. The Corbel Vault carries Unavailable <after discovering Arch Construction>.
CO05.conj: Stones stepped inward, course by course, until they meet.

CO06.name: Flying Buttress
CO06.fx: +15% Production when constructing University buildings in all cities — the masons who raised the cathedrals raised the colleges. Notre Dame, Taj Mahal, Porcelain Tower (world wonders). Walls that lean on air.
CO06.flav: Walls that lean on air: the masons who raised the cathedrals raised the colleges.

CO07.name: Earthquake-Resistant Design
CO07.fx: Timber-Frame Hall [75/1; +2 Gold (the technique sells); -25% maintenance cost for All buildings in this city; Must be on Hill]. Re-based on hill country (Civ V has no seismic zones).
CO07.conj: Timber that bends where stone would crack might ride out the earthquakes.

CO08.name: Modular Construction
CO08.fx: +25% Production when constructing All buildings in all cities — standard parts, everywhere.

CO09.name: Suspension Bridge
CO09.fx: +1 Gold from each Trade Route; +1 Production in all cities connected to capital — the canyon crossed, the network pays.
CO09.conj: A road hung from cables might cross a gorge no arch could span.

CO10.name: Iron-Frame Construction
CO10.fx: Factory (the canonical Industrialization building: +4 Production; Production +10%; Engineer ×2). The ruleset derivation gives the canonical Factory Remove Steam Works in this city: a Factory built where Steam Works stand converts them, twice as fast (the Steam Works' own clause), as a Steam Works converts an Engine House.

CO11.name: Reinforced Concrete
CO11.prereq: (CO04 or CH05) + ME12 — Roman Concrete, or the chemistry of Portland cement; and Bessemer steel
CO11.fx: +10% Production when constructing All buildings in all cities — steel and concrete build fast and stand hard; Improves movement speed on roads — the canonical Machinery unique, for cement roads. Dams become possible. Military Base; Bunker 325/2; requires a Military Base in this city; cityStrength +8; cityHealth +50 — detached forts in concrete and steel.
CO11.flav: Steel and concrete build fast and stand hard: Portland cement and Bessemer steel.

CO13.name: Geodesic Structures
CO13.fx: +15% Production when constructing Stadium buildings in all cities — the dome over the arena. Any climate, enclosed.
CO13.conj: A dome of light struts, all triangles, might roof an arena in any climate.

CO14.name: 3D Printed Construction
CO14.fx: +33% Production when constructing All buildings in all cities — printed, not built.

CO15.name: Orbital Construction
CO15.fx: Orbital Platform [560/3; +2 Production; +10% Production in this city — orbital industry; any city may have one]. Enables the Space Station and the large orbital projects.

CO23.name: Railway Network
CO23.prereq: MC08 (Steam Engine) + CO03 (Arch Construction — roads) + ME08 (Blast Furnace)
CO23.fx: Railroad (improvement — Civ V's built-in railroad connection bonus applies); Railway Station [60/0; +2 Gold, +1 Production from each Trade Route]; Neuschwanstein (world wonder). Distance stops mattering between connected cities.
CO23.flav: The defining infrastructure of the industrial age: distance stops mattering.

CO18.name: Coral Architecture
CO18.fx: Coral Walls [replaces Walls; 75/0; cityStrength +6; cityHealth +50; Must be next to Coast]; Reef Farm improvement on Atoll and Coast; 3 turns; +1 Food. Civ unique: +1 Food, +1 Production from Atoll tiles in all cities — the reef is quarry and larder.

CO19.name: Crannog Lake Dwelling
CO19.fx: Crannog [replaces Walls; 75/0; cityStrength +7; +1 Food from Lakes tiles in this city; Must be next to Lakes]. Civ unique: +1 Food from Marsh tiles in all cities — the fen that keeps out armies feeds the village.

CO20.name: Earthquake Mastery
CO20.fx: Seismic Pagoda [replaces Monument; 40/1; +2 Culture; cityStrength +4; -25% maintenance cost for All buildings in this city]. Civ unique: -15% maintenance cost for All buildings in all cities. Re-based on Hill and Mountain country (Civ V has no seismic zones): flexible frames that stand where stone falls.

CO21.name: Ceremonial Road Network
CO21.prereq: CO03 (Arch Construction — roads) + CU02 (Monumental Architecture) + Mountain or Jungle biome
CO21.fx: Pilgrimage Route improvement on Hill and Jungle; 5 turns; +1 Culture, +1 Faith; Sacred Way [national wonder; 100/0; +2 Culture, +2 Faith; +1 Culture from each Trade Route]. Civ unique: +1 Culture, +1 Faith in all cities connected to capital — every city the sacred road reaches shares the rite.
CO21.flav: Incan royal roads, Roman Via Sacra, Maya sacbeob.

CO22.name: Mound Builder Tradition
CO22.prereq: CO01 + SO03 (Tribal Law) + River + Grassland biome
CO22.fx: Earthen Mound national wonder; 75/0; +3 Culture, +2 Faith; Mound Platform 45/1; +1 Culture; cityStrength +4; cityHealth +25. Civ unique: +1 Culture from {River} {Grassland} tiles in all cities — the river plain remembers its builders.

CO24.name: Concentric Fortification
CO24.fx: Castle (and the Mughal Fort); Alhambra (world wonder) — rings of walls and flanking towers: defence in depth.
CO24.flav: Rings of walls and flanking towers: Krak des Chevaliers, Edward I’s Welsh castles.

CO25.name: Star Fort
CO25.fx: Arsenal; Kremlin (world wonder) — low, angled bastions that turn a bombardment aside.
CO25.flav: The trace italienne: low, angled bastions that turn a bombardment aside.

SF01.name: Reed/Log Raft
SF01.fx: Fishing Boats (improvement); Work Boats (unit). The coast becomes food.
SF01.conj: Logs float on the river; lashed together, they might carry us across.

SF02.name: Dugout Canoe
SF02.fx: Enables embarkation for land units (the canonical Optics unique — the first boats that carry people). River and shallow-water travel.

SF03.name: Sail Invention
SF03.fx: Lighthouse; The Great Lighthouse (world wonder); +1 Movement <for Embarked units> (sail on the transports). Port [40/1; +1 Gold; +1 Gold from Water resource tiles in this city; Must be next to Coast] — the sea pays before it connects (over-water connection arrives with the Harbor, SF08); the Phoenicians traded as soon as they sailed.

SF04.name: Celestial Navigation
SF04.fx: Enables Embarked units to enter ocean tiles (the canonical Astronomy unique — open ocean, new continents); Work Boats may enter ocean from here.

SF06.name: Polynesian Wayfinding
SF06.fx: Free Great Person (a Triggerable, once — the Wayfinder); Wayfinder's Hall [55/1; +1 Culture; +1 Food from Ocean tiles in this city]. Civ uniques: +1 Movement <for Water units> and +1 Sight <for Water units> — the stars, the swells and the birds are chart enough.

SF07.name: Viking Longship
SF07.fx: Longship [unit, Melee Water; cost 60; mv 5; str 12; Can carry 1 Land units — the raiding party aboard]. Civ uniques: +1 Movement <for Embarked units>; No movement cost to pillage (for Melee units). Rivers, coasts, and what lies on them.

SF08.name: Compass
SF08.fx: Harbor; +1 Movement <for Water units>. Never lost again.

SF09.name: Caravel/Deep Ocean Ship
SF09.fx: Caravel (unit). The far shore is reachable. Galleass (unit) — a hinged rudder on the centreline steers a far larger hull: the rudder made the great hulls possible.

SF10.name: Drydock
SF10.fx: Drydock [70/1; requires a Harbor in this city; +25% Production when constructing Water units in this city; Water Units adjacent to this city heal +10 HP per turn when healing; Must be next to Coast].

SF12.name: Ironclad
SF12.fx: Ironclad, Destroyer (units). Wooden navies are obsolete.
SF12.conj: A hull sheathed in iron plate might shrug off shot that splinters oak.

SF13.name: Submarine
SF13.prereq: SF12 + CO11 (Reinforced Concrete) + CH05 (Oxygen Theory) + OP01 (Glassmaking) + MC03 (Gearing)
SF13.fx: Submarine (unit — its base-game type is Invisible to non-adjacent units); +25% Production when constructing Submarine units in all cities — the sealed hull.

SF14.name: Nuclear Submarine
SF14.prereq: SF13 + (NP03 Nuclear Fission, or QM-E02 Bound-Energy Release)
SF14.fx: Nuclear Submarine, Missile Cruiser (units). In elemental worlds, where nothing is nuclear, it is named for its reactor as that world's science understands it: Quintessic Submarine (Substance) / Overcycle Submarine (Process).
SF14.flav: Elemental name: Quintessic Submarine (Substance) / Overcycle Submarine (Process).

SF15.name: Ekranoplan
SF15.fx: Ekranoplan [unit, Melee Water; cost 350; mv 8; str 35; Can carry 2 Land units; Double movement in Coast]. Enormous, fast, and never far above the waves. Also discoverable through Aeronautics.

SF16.name: Dhow Monsoon Trading
SF16.fx: Dhow [unit, Melee Water; cost 50; mv 5; str 8; +1 Sight; Withdraws before melee combat <with 80% chance>]; Monsoon Harbour [replaces Harbor; 120/3; Connects trade routes over water; +2 Gold from each Trade Route; +1 Production from Water resource tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Gold from {Coastal} {Desert} tiles in all cities — the monsoon shore is a market.

SF17.name: Reed Boat Mastery
SF17.prereq: SF01 + G02 + Lake/wetland or River biome
SF17.fx: Reed Boat unit, Melee Water; cost 30; mv 4; str 6; Cannot enter ocean tiles; Reed Village [replaces Monument; 40/1; +2 Culture; +1 Food from Lakes tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Production from Marsh tiles in all cities — the reeds are boat, house and fuel.
SF17.flav: Lake Titicaca, Marsh Arab ma'dan, Nile papyrus boats.

SF19.name: Longitude
SF19.fx: Seaport — a ship that knows where it is can use a port that is far away.
SF19.flav: Harrison's marine chronometer, 1761: a ship that always knows where it is.

WA01.name: Formation Fighting
WA01.fx: Spearman (unit); Barracks (and the Russian Krepost). Men who fight as one.

WA04.name: Composite Bow
WA04.fx: Composite Bowman (unit). With Horse Domestication, the Horse Archer line follows.

WA05.name: Siege Warfare
WA05.fx: Catapult (unit). Walls stop being final. (The Assyrian Battering Ram remains Assyria's, gated here.)

WA06.name: Fortification Design
WA06.fx: Fort (improvement); Great Wall (world wonder). (The Castle, Mughal Fort and Alhambra move to Concentric Fortification, CO24.)

WA07.name: Cavalry Tactics
WA07.fx: Horseman (unit); +10% to Flank Attack bonuses — riders who strike where the line bends.
WA07.flav: Riders who strike where the line bends.

WA08.name: Chariot Warfare
WA08.fx: Chariot Archer (unit). The Chariot Archer's obsoleteTech becomes Cavalry Tactics (set by the ruleset derivation).
WA08.conj: A light cart behind fast horses might carry a man with a bow into battle.

WA10.name: Gunpowder
WA10.fx: Musketman (unit — now requires Saltpeter); Himeji Castle (world wonder). Unlocks Cannons. Removed by GUNPOWDER_ABSENT. Discoverable through Chemistry or Warfare.

WA12.name: Greek Fire Naval Warfare
WA12.fx: Siphon Galley [unit, Ranged Water; cost 80; mv 4; str 12; ranged str 14; range 1; +50% Strength <vs Water units>]; +15% Strength <for Water units> <vs cities>. (Byzantium's Dromon remains Byzantine.)

WA13.name: Guerrilla Tactics
WA13.fx: All Land Military units gain the Guerrilla promotion (+25% Strength <when defending> <in Rough terrain tiles>); -25% Unhappiness from Population in annexed cities — occupiers find the hills expensive.
WA13.conj: Small bands who know the hills and forests might bleed a larger army.

WA14.name: Mongol Combined Arms
WA14.prereq: WA07 + WA04 + AH03 + WA27 (Stirrup) + Steppe/grassland biome
WA14.fx: Mangudai unit, Mounted ranged; cost 140; mv 5; str 12; ranged str 18; range 2; Can move after attacking; No defensive terrain bonus; requires Horses; Yam Station [replaces Stable; 100/1; +2 Unit Supply per city; +15% Production when constructing Mounted units in this city]. Civ unique: Great General provides double combat bonus — the khan's word reaches every horseman. (Mongolia's Keshik remains Mongol; a Mongol player who finds this stacks the two.)

WA17.name: Repeating Crossbow (Chu-Ko-Nu)
WA17.fx: Repeating Crossbowman [unit, Archery type; cost 130; mv 2; str 13; ranged str 16; range 2; 1 additional attacks per turn]. Dominant ranged unit of a GUNPOWDER_ABSENT world. (China's Chu-Ko-Nu remains Chinese.)
WA17.flav: Chinese-inspired. An exciting discovery when it appears.

WA18.name: Pneumatic Weaponry
WA18.fx: Air Rifleman [unit, Archery type — no Saltpeter needed; cost 200; mv 2; str 20; ranged str 24; range 2; +1 Sight]. Silent, and free of powder.
WA18.flav: What if the Girandoni air rifle lineage continued?

WA19.name: Railgun Concept
WA19.fx: Railgun Battery [unit, Siege; cost 400; mv 2; str 30; ranged str 45; range 3; +200% Strength <vs cities> <when attacking>; requires Aluminum]. Prerequisite for the Mass Driver.

WA20.name: Drone Warfare
WA20.fx: Drone [unit, Fighter type; cost 350; mv 1; str 30; ranged str 45; range 8; +2 Sight; requires Rare Earths]; Mechanized Infantry (unit); Pentagon (world wonder).

WA21.name: Powered Armor
WA21.fx: Giant Death Robot (unit — the exosuit taken to its conclusion; requires Uranium, as in the base game); +1 Movement <for Armored units>.

WA22.name: Cannons
WA22.prereq: WA10 (Gunpowder) + (ME05 (Steel Production — cast iron) or ME08 (Blast Furnace))
WA22.fx: Cannon (unit — requires Saltpeter). Medieval walls stop mattering.

WA23.name: Bushido Warrior Code
WA23.prereq: WA01 + WA03 (Archery — the samurai bow) + (ME06 (Damascus/Wootz Steel) or ME05) + Island or Coastal biome
WA23.fx: Bushido Dojo [replaces Barracks; 75/1; New Melee units start with 30 XP in this city; +1 Culture]. Civ uniques: Earn 50% of killed Military unit's Strength as Culture (every honourable victory is remembered) and +10% Strength <for Melee units> <when defending> (the code does not retreat). No unit is granted — Japan's Samurai remains Japanese; a Japanese player who finds this stacks code on steel.

WA24.name: Fortified Border Tradition
WA24.prereq: WA06 (Fortification Design) + CO02 + Many neighbors modifier
WA24.fx: Gatehouse replaces Walls; 75/0; cityStrength +6; +2 Gold — tolls at the chokepoint. Civ unique: Enemy Land units must spend 1 extra movement points when inside your territory (the Great Wall's own unique, made a culture).

WA25.name: Berserker Tradition
WA25.fx: Huscarl [unit, Melee; cost 120; mv 2; str 21; +25% Strength <when attacking>; starts with the Amphibious promotion]; Mead Hall [replaces Barracks; 75/1; +1 Culture; cityStrength +3; New Military units start with 15 XP in this city]. Civ unique: +50% Yield from pillaging tiles — raiding pays. (Denmark's Berserker remains Danish.)

WA26.name: Professional Army
WA26.fx: Terracotta Army (world wonder); Heroic Epic (national wonder) — a standing army, paid, drilled and remembered.
WA26.flav: The Marian reforms (107 BC): soldiers by trade, not by levy.

WA27.name: Stirrup
WA27.fx: Knight (unit) — the rider braced to strike with his whole weight.
WA27.flav: The stirrup spread west across Eurasia between the 6th and 8th centuries.

WA28.name: Drill and Discipline
WA28.fx: Military Academy; Brandenburg Gate (world wonder); Cavalry and Lancer (units) — needing no gunpowder, so cavalry keeps its long relevance in gunpowder-less worlds; +25% Strength <for Gunpowder units> <vs Mounted units> — pike and shot in one formation.
WA28.flav: Maurice of Nassau’s drill (1590s), written from the classical manuals.

MA01.name: Geometry
MA01.fx: -25% construction time for All improvements — surveyed land is improved faster. Prerequisite for the Arch and Mechanics. +1 Gold from all Market buildings — place value keeps the market's accounts: arithmetic and geometry together, as in Babylon and Alexandria.
MA01.flav: Surveyed land is improved faster; place value keeps the market’s accounts.

MA03.name: Basic Algebra
MA03.fx: +5% Production when constructing All buildings in all cities — engineering by calculation. +10% Strength <for Siege units> (artillery by angle); +1 Culture from all World Wonder buildings (proportion in stone) — algebra and trigonometry, the mathematics of Alexandria and Baghdad.
MA03.flav: Algebra and trigonometry, the mathematics of Alexandria and Baghdad.

MA05.name: Calculus
MA05.prereq: MA03 + O06 (Natural Philosophy) + PH04 (Scientific Method — the new mechanics it was made for)
MA05.fx: Unlocks Mechanics focus (advanced); +1 Range <for Siege units> (trajectories solved); +15% Insight to the physical foci.
MA05.flav: Trajectories solved: the path of a shot worked out before it is fired.

MA06.name: Probability Theory
MA06.prereq: MA03 + SO11 (Banking — insurance and the merchant's risk)
MA06.fx: +1 Gold from all Bank buildings — insurance priced by probability. +10% Gold in all cities — risk, priced and pooled.
MA06.flav: Insurance priced by probability: risk, priced and pooled.

MA07.name: Binary Mathematics
MA07.fx: Cipher Office [60/0; +25% spy effectiveness in this city (<when espionage is enabled>)]. Prerequisite for Computing.

MA08.name: Non-Euclidean Geometry
MA08.fx: +10% Gold from Trade Routes — accurate maps, shortest paths. Prerequisite for Relativity.

MA09.name: Statistics
MA09.fx: +5% Production in all cities — quality control.
MA09.flav: Quality control: a factory’s output judged from a sample.

MA11.name: Fractal Mathematics
MA11.prereq: MA05 + MA08 + CP01 (Programmable Computer — Mandelbrot's plots)
MA11.fx: +1 Science from Mine tiles in all cities — terrain read as mathematics.
MA11.conj: Coastlines and mountains might follow a mathematics of their own.

MA12.name: Mayan Vigesimal Mathematics
MA12.fx: Long Count Observatory 55/1; +2 Science, +1 Faith; +10% Insight to Observation. Civ unique: +1 Science from Jungle tiles in all cities — the calendar is kept in the canopy.

MA13.name: Topology
MA13.fx: +1 Gold, +1 Production from each Trade Route — the network optimised. -10% maintenance cost for All buildings in all cities — administration by set and rule: Cantor and Poincaré, the new mathematics of the same decades.
MA13.flav: Administration by set and rule: Cantor and Poincaré, the new mathematics.

MA14.name: Chaos Theory
MA14.fx: +5% growth in all cities (long-range forecasting for the fields); +10% to Flank Attack bonuses (positioning solved).

MA15.name: Optimisation Theory
MA15.prereq: MA13 + MA09 + CP01 (Programmable Computer — linear programming ran on computers) — **cost ×2.5**
MA15.fx: -15% maintenance cost for All buildings in all cities, on top of MA13's −10%.

MA16.name: Operations Research
MA16.fx: -25% maintenance costs (unit upkeep; to confirm against Unciv).

MA17.name: Lifecycle Engineering
MA17.fx: -33% Gold cost of upgrading — retrofits planned from the start.

MA22.name: Auction Theory
MA22.fx: Gold cost of purchasing items in cities -15%.

MA23.name: Post-Quantum Cryptography
MA23.fx: +5% Gold in all cities (secure finance); -25% enemy spy effectiveness in all cities <when espionage is enabled>.

MA20.name: Computational Proof
MA20.fx: -10% Science cost of researching new Technologies.

MA21.name: Automated Mathematics
MA21.fx: -15% Science cost of researching new Technologies, +10% Science in all cities.

CU04.name: Musical Instruments
CU04.fx: Great Prophet is earned +10% faster — music in ritual and worship. (Culture-spreading bards have no Unciv mechanism.)

CU12.name: Sacred Dance Tradition
CU12.prereq: CU04 (Musical Instruments) + SO02 + Tropical or Desert biome
CU12.fx: Dance Ground replaces Monument; 40/1; +2 Culture, +1 Faith, +1 Happiness. Civ unique: +1 Happiness in all cities <in cities with a Dance Ground> — cohesion in every city that dances.
CU12.flav: West African, Aboriginal Australian, Native American ceremonial dance.

CU13.name: Talking Drum Networks
CU13.fx: Drum Tower [10/0; +1 Culture; Must have an owned Forest within 2 tiles]. Civ unique: Resting point for Influence with City-States is increased by 10 — every neighbour hears the drums.
CU13.flav: West African-inspired. Relocated from the former Communications focus.

CU02.name: Monumental Architecture
CU02.fx: Temple (and the Egyptian Burial Tomb and Songhai Mud Pyramid Mosque that replace it). Monumental faith. (Hagia Sophia, the Great Mosque of Djenne and the Grand Temple move to the University, CU06, their Medieval era.) -25% Culture cost of natural border growth in all cities — the stones mark whose land this is. Stonehenge, The Pyramids, Mausoleum of Halicarnassus (world wonders) — the first monuments, and the first alignments with the sky.

CU03.name: Artistic Tradition
CU03.fx: Great Artist is earned +10% faster — a tradition that trains its own masters. (The Hermitage moves to the Renaissance, CU07; the Louvre and the Museum to The Enlightenment, PH14; the National Epic to Historiography, CU14.)

CU10.name: Sacred River Tradition
CU10.fx: River Temple [replaces Temple; 100/2; requires a Shrine in this city; +2 Faith, +1 Culture; +1 Food from River tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Faith from River tiles in all cities — the river is holy, and it feeds you.
CU10.flav: Ganges, Nile, Tigris-Euphrates sacred river traditions.

PH01.name: Formal Logic
PH01.fx: Gifts of Gold to City-States generate +25% more Influence — the structured argument persuades. +1 Science from every specialist in all cities; -25% enemy spy effectiveness in all cities (<when espionage is enabled>) — scepticism as defence: Aristotle's logic and his account of knowledge.

PH12.name: Harmonious Inquiry
PH12.prereq: O06 (Natural Philosophy) + Diverse biome (3+ terrain types)
PH12.fx: Academy of Harmony [100/1; +2 Science, +1 Culture; +1 Science for every known Natural Wonder]. Civ unique: +2 Science for every known Natural Wonder — inquiry that walks the whole world. (Approximates the design's per-terrain-type bonus, which has no direct template.)
PH12.flav: Chinese natural philosophy, Greek peripatetic tradition.

CU05.name: Theater
CU05.fx: Amphitheater; the drama festival via Events.json. (The Opera House, the Celtic Ceilidh Hall, the Sistine Chapel and the Theatre belong to the Renaissance, CU07.)

CU06.name: University
CU06.fx: University (and the Siamese Wat); Angkor Wat (world wonder); Oxford University. (The theology wonders are Scholastic Theology's, CU15.)
CU06.flav: Bologna (1088), Paris and Oxford (12th c.), three centuries before the press.

CU11.name: Courtly Love Tradition
CU11.fx: Royal Court replaces Amphitheater; 100/2; requires a Monument in this city; +3 Culture; Great Artist points 2. Civ unique: When declaring friendship, both parties gain a 15% boost to great person generation — courtship, made diplomacy.

PH04.name: Scientific Method
PH04.prereq: PH01 + CU06 (University — the schools where natural philosophy was taught) + MC06 (Printing Press — observations fixed, shared and checked)
PH04.fx: +25% Science in all cities — Insight is science, so the design's game-changing bonus is this one legal unique. Experimental Laboratory 190/2; requires a University in this city; +2 Science; Scientist ×1 — the experiment as institution.

CU07.name: Renaissance
CU07.fx: Empire enters a 10-turn Golden Age (a Triggerable on discovery — the Renaissance itself); Hermitage (national wonder); Opera House (and the Celtic Ceilidh Hall); Theatre; Sistine Chapel (world wonder) — music and drama for a paying public: opera began in Renaissance Florence, and the Sistine ceiling dates from 1512.

PH09.name: Existentialism
PH09.prereq: PH01 (Formal Logic — epistemology) + PH14 (The Enlightenment — the rational order it answered)
PH09.fx: +2 Culture from every Artist — the movement finds its voices. Existential-crisis events via Events.json.
PH09.conj: If life has no given purpose, each of us may have to make one.

PH10.name: Information Theory
PH10.prereq: PH01 + MA07 (Binary Math) + EN01 (Vacuum Tube — the telephone and radio circuits it measured)
PH10.fx: Great Scientist is earned +10% faster — information made measurable. Prerequisite for Computing.
PH10.conj: Information itself might be measured, counted out in yes-or-no answers.

PH11.name: Systems Thinking
PH11.fx: +5% Production in all cities; +5% growth in all cities — the whole seen as a system.
PH11.conj: A city, a market or a forest might be understood only as a whole.

CU14.name: Historiography
CU14.fx: National Epic (national wonder) — the past written down, and argued over.
CU14.flav: Herodotus and Thucydides wrote their histories in the 5th century BC.

CU15.name: Scholastic Theology
CU15.fx: Hagia Sophia, Great Mosque of Djenne (world wonders); Grand Temple (national wonder) — faith argued by logic.
CU15.flav: In the age of Aquinas and the kalam, faith was argued by logic.

PH14.name: The Enlightenment
PH14.fx: Museum; The Louvre (world wonder) — knowledge gathered, ordered and shown.
PH14.flav: The British Museum was founded in 1753; the Encyclopédie began to appear in 1751.

MD01.name: Surgical Techniques
MD01.fx: Surgery [20/0; requires a Herbalist in this city; Military Units adjacent to this city heal +10 HP per turn when healing].
MD01.flav: Trepanation is Neolithic: surgery predates comparative anatomy by millennia.

MD02.name: Quarantine Protocols
MD02.fx: Quarantine Station [25/0; +10% growth in this city].

MD03.name: Anatomy Study
MD03.prereq: O03 (Animal Behavior Study) + G03 (Herbal Medicine) + O06 (Natural Philosophy — Alcmaeon's and Aristotle's dissections)
MD03.fx: Medical School [50/1; requires a Library in this city; Scientist ×1; Military Units adjacent to this city heal +5 HP per turn when healing]. Foundation of advanced medicine. The body learned by dissection, animal first: Aristotle compared animals, Herophilus dissected human bodies at Alexandria, and Galen's anatomy was largely of apes and pigs.

MD04.name: Vaccination
MD04.prereq: MD03 + AH02 (Herd Animal Domestication — the milkmaid observation) + PH04 (Scientific Method — Jenner's trial)
MD04.fx: +10% growth in all cities — the plague years end. Also discoverable through Animal Husbandry (the milkmaid observation).
MD04.flav: The milkmaid observation: the plague years end.

MD05.name: Germ Theory
MD05.prereq: MD03 + PH04 (Scientific Method) + OP03 (Telescope — the microscope)

MD06.name: Antibiotics
MD06.fx: Medical Lab; All newly-trained Military units in all cities receive the Medic promotion. Germ-exclusive. Grants MASS_MEDICINE (germ route). The primary of the infection Competing Solution; Phage Therapy is its alternative. The canonical Medical Lab gains Remove Phage Institute in this city through the ruleset derivation: a city holds one or the other, and switches by building the other.
MD06.flav: The magic bullet — but only if microbes are the enemy.
MD06.conj: A compound that kills germs but spares the patient might cure infection.

MD07.name: Anaesthesia
MD07.prereq: MD01 + CH04 (Distillation) + CH05 (Oxygen Theory — the pneumatic chemists' gases)
MD07.fx: +5 HP when healing — surgery in the field.
MD07.conj: Distilled vapours might put a patient beyond pain while the surgeon works.

MD08.name: Prosthetics
MD08.fx: All newly-trained Land units in all cities receive the Medic promotion — the wounded return to the line. Prerequisite for Cybernetic Enhancement.
MD08.conj: Geared limbs of wood and metal might send the wounded back to the line.

MD09.name: Trepanation Tradition
MD09.fx: +15% Great Person generation in all cities (lives lengthened); +1 Culture in capital.
MD09.flav: What if early trepanation led to neurosurgical tradition?

MD10.name: Traditional Medicine Integration
MD10.prereq: G03 + MD03 + Diverse biome (3+ terrain types)
MD10.fx: Apothecary [75/1; +1 Happiness, +1 Gold; Military Units adjacent to this city heal +10 HP per turn when healing]. Civ unique: +1 Happiness in all cities; +25% Insight to Medicine.

MD11.name: Gene Therapy
MD11.prereq: GN03 (Genetic Engineering) + MASS_MEDICINE token (MD06 germ, MD18 humoral, or MD16 miasma)
MD11.fx: +25% Great Person generation in all cities (long lives); the Designer Baby choice via Events.json.

MD12.name: Cybernetic Enhancement
MD12.fx: All Military units gain the Augmented promotion (+10% Strength); +1 Production from every specialist in all cities; augmentation dilemmas via Events.json.

MD13.name: Cryogenic Preservation
MD13.fx: Cryo Chamber [190/1; +25% Great Person generation in this city].

MD14.name: Hot Spring Healing Tradition
MD14.prereq: G03 (Herbal Medicine) + Volcanic region or Mountain biome
MD14.fx: Thermal Bath [55/1; +2 Happiness, +1 Culture; Must be on Hill or Must have an owned Volcanic within 2 tiles]; Hot Spring improvement on Hill and Volcanic; 5 turns; +1 Gold, +1 Culture. Civ unique: +1 Happiness in cities on Hill tiles.
MD14.flav: Japanese onsen, Roman thermae, Icelandic hot springs.

MD15.name: Contagion Experiments
MD15.fx: Contagion Laboratory [national wonder; 200/0; +2 Science; on completion Triggers a Contagion Experiments event and Reveals this world's medicine: Germ Theory (MD05, ~60%), Miasma Engineering (MD16, ~20%) or Humoral Medicine (MD17, ~20%)]. Clear report either way.
MD15.flav: Pasteur’s swan-neck flask, and controlled exposure.

MD20.name: Phage Therapy
MD20.prereq: MD05 (Germ Theory validated) + OP03 (Telescope — the microscope)
MD20.fx: Phage Institute [250/1; requires a Hospital in this city; +15% growth in this city; 15% Food is carried over after population increases in this city; Remove Medical Lab in this city] — a library of bacteriophages, each matched to one strain. (the phage route). The trade: no empire-wide effect — antibiotics are broad, cheap and mass-produced, and that is why they usually win; phages must be matched city by city, and an Institute occupies the slot a Medical Lab would. What phag
MD20.flav: Félix d'Hérelle was treating infections with phages in the 1920s; the Eliava Institute in Tbilisi kept the practice alive after the West chose penicillin, and resistance has brought it back.
MD20.conj: Viruses that prey on bacteria might be bred to fight infection.

MD21.name: Engineered Phages
MD21.fx: +15% growth in all cities <in cities with a Phage Institute> — phages designed rather than found: the Institutes double in worth. The late payoff for the harder road, and only for cities that took it.

TR01.name: Barter System
TR01.fx: +1 Gold from each Trade Route — city connections begin to pay the moment roads exist. The Trade screen (UI).

TR02.name: Currency
TR02.fx: Market (and the Arabian Bazaar). Standard coin, standard price.

TR03.name: Caravansary
TR03.fx: Caravansary [45/1; +1 Gold; +1 Gold from each Trade Route; +1 Gold from Desert tiles in this city].

TR05.name: Letter of Credit
TR05.prereq: TR02 + SO04 + SO11 (Banking — the houses that honoured the bill)
TR05.fx: +25% Gold from Trade Routes — value travels without the coin.

TR06.name: Joint Stock Company
TR06.fx: Trading Company [375/3; requires a Bank in this city; +3 Gold; Merchant ×2; +2 Gold from each Trade Route].

TR08.name: Cowrie Shell Currency
TR08.fx: Cowrie Exchange [replaces Market; 100/0; +2 Gold; Gold +25%; Merchant ×1; +1 Gold from Coast tiles in this city] — satisfies Currency's Copper Working prerequisite. Civ unique: +1 Gold from Coast tiles in all cities — money you can pick up on the beach.
TR08.flav: West African/South Asian/Chinese alternative economic path.

TR09.name: Free Trade Agreements
TR09.fx: Stock Exchange; Enables Research agreements (the canonical unique) — treaties that trade knowledge as well as goods.

TR10.name: Futures Market
TR10.fx: Commodity Exchange [625/3; requires a Bank in this city; +4 Gold; +1 Gold from Strategic resource tiles in this city].
TR10.conj: A price might be agreed today for a harvest not yet sown.

TR11.name: Caravan Oasis Network
TR11.fx: Grand Caravanserai [replaces Caravansary; 40/1; +1 Gold; +2 Gold from each Trade Route; +1 Food, +1 Gold from Oasis tiles in this city]; Oasis Rest Stop improvement on Desert; 4 turns; +1 Food, +1 Gold. Civ unique: +1 Gold from Desert tiles in all cities — the empty land is a road with tolls.
TR11.flav: Silk Road, Trans-Saharan trade, Arabian caravanserai.

TR12.name: Potlatch Economy
TR12.fx: Potlatch Hall replaces Monument; 40/1; +2 Culture, +1 Happiness; Great Merchant points 2. Civ unique: +1 Happiness from each type of luxury resource — wealth given away comes back as standing.

TR14.name: Bazaar Economy
TR14.prereq: TR01 + SO06 (Codified Law) + Desert/arid or Many neighbors biome
TR14.fx: Souk replaces Market; 100/0; +2 Gold; Gold +25%; Merchant ×2. Civ unique: +10% Gold from Trade Routes and +1 Happiness from each type of luxury resource — a market that thrives on variety. (Arabia's Bazaar remains Arabian.)

TR15.name: Post-Scarcity Economics
TR15.prereq: MC12 (Robotics) + (ES08 Fusion, or ES12 Zero-Point, or ES14 Adv. Fission, or QM-E05 Re-Tempering Reactor, or QM-E07 Aether Tension Engine)
TR15.fx: -100% maintenance cost for All buildings in all cities; +3 Happiness in all cities — scarcity ends, and with it the bill.

TR17.name: Long-Distance Trade
TR17.fx: Petra (world wonder); Trading post (improvement) — the routes that cross a continent.
TR17.conj: Passed from caravan to caravan, goods might cross a whole continent.

TX01.name: Weaving
TX01.fx: Weaver 10/0; +1 Gold. Cloth, sails and leather for the bellows (ME-B). Wool spun and worn: +1 Production from Sheep tiles in all cities; +1 Happiness in cities on Tundra tiles.

TX02.name: Dyeing
TX02.fx: Dye Works [45/1; +2 Gold; +1 Gold from Dyes tiles in this city].

TX03.name: Silk Production
TX03.fx: Silk Weavers [replaces Weaver; 95/1; +2 Gold, +1 Culture; Provides 1 Silk — the base luxury, made rather than found]. Civ uniques: +2 Gold from each Trade Route and +1 Culture from each Trade Route — the Silk Road carries more than silk.

TX05.name: Cotton Gin
TX05.fx: Textile Mill [220/2; requires a Weaver in this city; +2 Gold; Engineer ×1; +1 Gold from Cotton tiles in this city].

TX08.name: Carbon Fiber
TX08.fx: +10% Strength <for Air units> — the cable that reaches orbit. All newly-trained Land units in all cities receive the Flak Jacket promotion (Flak Jacket: +15% Strength <when defending> <vs Ranged units>) — two engineered fibres of the same years.
TX08.conj: Threads of pure carbon, set in resin, might prove stronger than steel.

TX10.name: Paper Making
TX10.prereq: TX01 + (WM01 (Canal — water processing) or F02 (Kiln Construction — bark processing))
TX10.fx: +15% Production when constructing Library buildings in all cities — cheap paper, cheap books. Prerequisite for the Printing Press.

TX11.name: Tapa Cloth Tradition
TX11.fx: Tapa Workshop [replaces Weaver; 30/1; +2 Culture; Great Artist points 2; +1 Culture from Jungle tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Culture from Jungle tiles in all cities — the bark is the canvas.

TX12.name: Imperial Dye Mastery
TX12.fx: Imperial Dye Works [replaces Dye Works; 110/1; +3 Gold, +2 Culture; Provides 1 Dyes]. Civ unique: +2 Gold, +1 Culture from Dyes tiles in all cities — purple is power.
TX12.flav: Phoenician purple, Indian indigo, Mesoamerican cochineal.

WM01.name: Canal Building
WM01.fx: Unlocks the Water Management chain. +1 Production in cities on River tiles (barge and mill-race); +1 Gold from each Trade Route (bulk goods by water). (Civ V has no canal improvement; the connection is abstracted.)

WM02.name: Aqueduct
WM02.fx: Aqueduct; Hanging Gardens (world wonder). Remove Marsh (improvement; and the Dutch Polder is gated here); draining is one use of a bog — Turbary offers the other, cutting it for peat; +1 Food from Flood plains tiles in all cities — the river kept in its bed.

WM03.name: Qanat System
WM03.fx: Qanat [replaces Aqueduct; 100/1; 40% Food is carried over after population increases in this city; +1 Food from Desert tiles in this city; needs no fresh water]. Civ unique: +1 Food from Desert tiles in all cities — water that never sees the sun.

WM05.name: Water Mill
WM05.fx: Water Mill. Also discoverable through Energy Systems.

WM06.name: Dam Construction
WM06.prereq: WM02 (Aqueduct — flood control) + CO11 (Reinforced Concrete) + EL06 (Electric Generator)
WM06.fx: +1 Food from River tiles in all cities — reservoirs that water the fields. Hydro Plant (canonical — requires Aluminum, must be on a River, +1 Production from River tiles; not a grid plant, so it stands beside one, as in Civ V) — the dam and its turbines.
WM06.conj: A wall of concrete across the valley might hold back the whole river.

WM07.name: Desalination
WM07.fx: Desalination Plant [125/1; +1 Food from Desert tiles in this city; Must be next to Coast] — the desert coast becomes a garden.

WM08.name: Stepwell Architecture
WM08.fx: Stepwell [65/1; +1 Food, +1 Culture, +1 Happiness; +1 Food from Desert tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Happiness in cities on Desert tiles — cool stone, deep water, and shade.

WM09.name: Rice Paddy Mastery
WM09.prereq: FA01 + WM01 + River biome + Tropical or Temperate biome
WM09.fx: Paddy Field improvement on Marsh and on Grassland or Plains beside a River; 6 turns; +2 Food; Rice Granary [replaces Granary; 60/1; +2 Food; +1 Food from Marsh tiles in this city]. Civ unique: +1 Food from Paddy Field tiles in all cities — the valley feeds a multitude.
WM09.flav: The rice civilisations of East and Southeast Asia.

WM10.name: Ice Architecture
WM10.fx: Ice Hall [replaces Walls; 75/0; cityStrength +5; +1 Food from Snow tiles in this city]. Civ uniques: +1 Production from Snow tiles in all cities; No Maintenance costs for improvements in Snow tiles; No Maintenance costs for improvements in Tundra tiles (the ice roads). Building with what the cold provides.

WM11.name: Industrial Canal Network
WM11.prereq: WM01 (Canal Building) + CO03 (Arch Construction) + TR03 (Caravansary) + TR06 (Joint Stock Company — the canal companies' capital) + River biome
WM11.fx: Pound Lock [60/0; +2 Gold, +2 Production from each Trade Route; Must be on River] — one horse pulls thirty tons. Requires River. The Pound Lock carries Unavailable <after discovering Railway Network>.
WM11.flav: Canal Mania, 1790s: one horse pulled 30 tons by barge, but only 1 ton by road cart.

WM12.name: Tidal Mill
WM12.fx: Tidal Mill [35/0; Must be next to Coast; +2 Food, +1 Production in this city <in cities without a Water Mill>] — a mill for a coast with no river: it yields the Water Mill's own output, and never alongside one.
WM12.flav: Northern Ireland (7th c.) to the Thames (11th c.).
WM12.conj: Sea water trapped behind a sluice gate might turn a wheel as a river does.

MC03.name: Gearing
MC03.fx: -25% construction time for Mine improvements — geared hoists and windlasses sink the shafts faster. Gears turn everything that follows; the Workshop comes with the crank that turns their motion to work. -25% construction time for Farm improvements — the seed drill is a geared machine, Han-era in China. +10% Production when constructing All wonders in all cities — the crane lifts what the arm cannot: lever, pulley and gear together, as in Hellenistic mechanics.
MC03.flav: The crane lifts what the arm cannot.

MC04.name: Windmill
MC04.fx: Windmill — the mill for country with no river to turn one. Where there is no Water Mill, it drives the industrial chain in its place: the crank, the Blast Furnace's bellows, Plate Armour's hammers and the Steam Engine's gearing. Also discoverable through Energy Systems.

MC05.name: Clockwork
MC05.fx: Great Engineer is earned +10% faster — the clockmaker, the first precision engineer.
MC05.flav: The clockmaker, the first precision engineer.

MC06.name: Printing Press
MC06.fx: +10% Science in all cities (Insight is science); Leaning Tower of Pisa (world wonder). Switches Knowledge Diffusion to its post-press phase (Section 1.2). The most important breakthrough in the game.
MC06.flav: Most important breakthrough in the game.

MC07.name: Hero's Aeolipile (Early Steam)
MC07.fx: Unlocks Thermodynamics focus, centuries early; Steam Temple 100/1; +2 Faith, +1 Culture, +1 Production. Seed of the Early Steam chain (TH13/TH14).
MC07.flav: What if Hero of Alexandria's steam engine was taken seriously?

MC08.name: Steam Engine
MC08.prereq: ME08 (Blast Furnace — coal or charcoal) + (WM05 or MC04 — the millwright's gearing and shafts) + PH04 (Scientific Method — the air-pump physics of Boyle and Papin)
MC08.fx: Steam Works [250/2; requires a Workshop in this city; +2 Production; Engineer ×1; Remove Engine House in this city; +100% Production when constructing Factory buildings in this city — built where an Engine House stands, it converts it]; Big Ben (world wonder); unlocks Thermodynamics if not already open. Prerequisite for the Railway.
MC08.flav: Watt's separate condenser (1769) began as a repair to a model Newcomen engine.

MC09.name: Internal Combustion Engine
MC09.fx: Landship, Tank, Anti-Tank Gun (units — Tank requires Oil; the Landship and Tank take this row as their requiredTech). Distillery Fuel Depot [375/2; requires a Distillery in this city; Provides 1 Oil <when number of [Worked Farm Tiles in this city] is more than 2>; -20% growth in this city <when number of [Worked Farm Tiles in this city] is more than 2>] — grain into spirit, only while its city works at least three Farms; ethanol counts as Oil, so it fuels any tank, battleship
MC09.flav: Fuel-starved Europe ran its cars on alcohol and wood gas in the Second World War.

MC10.name: Precision Machining
MC10.fx: Great War Infantry (unit); Statue of Liberty (world wonder); +10% Production when constructing Military units in all cities — interchangeable parts.

MC11.name: Assembly Line
MC11.fx: Machine Gun (unit) — the line moves, the workers stand; +15% Production when constructing All buildings in all cities; +25% Production when constructing Military Base buildings in all cities — buildings made on the line, too: forward bases in weeks.
MC11.flav: The line moves; the workers stand.

MC12.name: Robotics
MC12.fx: Spaceship Factory; -25% construction time for All improvements (robot labour). Prerequisite for AI and Orbital Assembly.

MC13.name: Perpetual Motion Understanding
MC13.fx: +1 Production from all Water Mill buildings; +1 Production from all Windmill buildings — knowing what cannot be done makes every engine better; +15% Insight to Thermodynamics and Energy.

MC14.name: Babbage Mechanical Computer
MC14.fx: Difference Engine [national wonder; 250/0; +4 Science; +10% Science in this city]; opens the Computing focus without electricity. Cost halved if any Antikythera (O13–O15) or Clockwork (MC15/MC16) breakthrough is known.

MC15.name: Mainspring Energy Storage
MC15.fx: Clockwork Toy Works 105/1; +1 Happiness, +2 Gold; +1 Production in all cities <in cities without a Water Mill> — spring power where water gives none. In ENHANCED_SPRINGS worlds the whole Clockwork path is dramatically more viable.
MC15.flav: What if metallurgy produced springs that stored far more energy?

MC16.name: Clockwork Automaton
MC16.fx: Automaton [unit, Civilian; cost 90; mv 2; Can build Land improvements on tiles; -100% maintenance costs — needs no pay]; Automated Workshop [105/1; requires a Workshop in this city; +2 Production; +1 Production from every specialist in this city]; The Mechanical Turk world wonder; 250; +3 Culture, +2 Science; Great Scientist points 2. Halves the cost of MC14.

MC17.name: Spring-Powered Vehicle
MC17.fx: +1 Movement <for Civilian units> — wind it at the city and drive until it stops. In ENHANCED_SPRINGS worlds these rival early steam and need no fuel at all.
MC17.flav: Range limited by spring tension — unless springs are better than expected.

MC18.name: Clockwork Analytical Engine
MC18.fx: Analytical Engine [national wonder; 300/0; +6 Science; +15% Science in this city]; opens the Computing focus with no electrical prerequisite. The clockwork computing path — slower than silicon, centuries earlier.

MC19.name: Crank and Connecting Rod
MC19.prereq: MC03 (Gearing) + (WM05 or MC04 — a water or wind mill to turn the crank)
MC19.fx: Workshop (and the Iroquois Longhouse) — rotation turned into strokes: mills that saw, hammer and pump. CORE because Unciv's Factory requires the Workshop, and every power plant the Factory.
MC19.flav: Al-Jazari (1206): rotation turned into strokes, for mills that saw, hammer and pump.

TH01.name: Laws of Thermodynamics
TH01.fx: +1 Production from all Steam Works buildings — the engine understoodif the kinetic account validates.
TH01.flav: The kinetic theory of heat: heat is motion.

TH02.name: Refrigeration
TH02.fx: Stadium; 15% Food is carried over after population increases in all cities — nothing spoils. +1 Gold from all Factory buildings — industrial gases, liquefied and sold: Linde built the refrigerator and then liquefied air. Liquid gases: rocket oxidiser, the superconductor path, cold storage.
TH02.flav: Linde built the refrigerator and then liquefied air.

TH03.name: Turbine Design
TH03.fx: +15% Production when constructing Water units in all cities — turbine-driven ships. Prerequisite for every power plant. +1 Happiness in cities on Snow tiles (district heating) — turbines and heat exchangers, the steam plant's two halves; prerequisite for reactors.

TH15.name: Waste-Heat Recovery
TH15.conj: The heat our factories throw away might be caught and set to work.

TH16.name: Heat Pump Networks
TH16.fx: +1 Production per 4 population in all cities.

TH17.name: Supercritical Power Cycles
TH17.fx: +1 Production from all Power Plant buildings.

TH18.name: Deep Cryogenics
TH18.fx: +15% Food is carried over after population increases, stacking with TH02's.

TH19.name: Permafrost Engineering
TH19.fx: A worker-built improvement that, <upon building> it, will Turn this tile into a Plains tile on tundra (to be tested in play). A civilisation without tundra never becomes eligible, so never wastes a discovery on it.

TH22.name: Geoengineering Programme
TH22.fx: +15% Food in all cities — a stabilised climate and reliable harvests (if the fork gains a disaster mechanic, reducing disasters is its natural effect).

TH05.name: Carnot Efficiency
TH05.fx: +1 Production from every Engineer — the engineer who knows the limit gets closest to it. Knowing the limit gets you closest to it.
TH05.flav: The engineer who knows the limit gets closest to it.

TH08.name: Stirling Engine Mastery
TH08.fx: Stirling Works [a grid plant: Power Plant (tag); 60/0; requires a Factory in this city; +1 Production; burns anything, needs no resource; Remove [{Power Plant} {non-Stirling Works}] in this city] — the earliest and weakest plant, fuel-free, holding a city's plant slot until something better is worth the swap.
TH08.flav: Less power, but it burns anything.

TH09.name: Caloric Theory
TH09.flav: Heat as a weightless fluid — wrong in our world.

TH10.name: Mechanical Equivalent of Heat
TH10.fx: Joule Laboratory [national wonder; 200/0; +2 Science; on completion Triggers a Mechanical Equivalent of Heat event and Reveals the heat this world has: Turbine Design in Kinetic worlds (~70%), the Caloric Reservoir in Caloric worlds (~30%)].
TH10.flav: Joule’s paddle-wheel and Rumford’s cannon: friction makes heat without limit.

TH13.name: The Weight of the Air
TH13.fx: Condensing Pump [50/1; +1 Happiness; +10% growth in this city] — steam condensed in a closed vessel leaves a vacuum, and the air pushes water in behind it: water raised a few metres from any well or stream, for the city's houses and fountains.
TH13.flav: Hero's Pneumatica opens, after Strato, by arguing that small vacua exist — the idea Aristotle's horror vacui denied, and the one our own history had to wait for Torricelli and Guericke to supply. This is Savery's pump (1698) without the pressure stage that burst its boilers. Savery sold it as The Mi

TH14.name: Atmospheric Engine
TH14.prereq: TH13 + (ME02 or ME05 — bronze or cast iron for the cylinder) + MC03 (Gearing — the lever and the beam)
TH14.fx: Engine House [175/1; requires a Workshop in this city; Consumes 1 Coal; +1 Production from Mine tiles in this city; +2 Food, +1 Production in this city <in cities without a Water Mill>; Unavailable <after discovering Steam Engine>; +100% Production when constructing Steam Works buildings in this city] — a beam engine that drains deep workings and, where no river turns a wheel, pumps water back over one: a mill away from the river. Stationary, reciprocating and ruinous on fuel
TH14.flav: Newcomen's engine (1712) never ran above about one atmosphere: the air did the work, and a piston sealed with leather and a layer of water hid a poor bore, so it needed no machining. It paid only at the pithead, burning coal no one could sell, and in the mid-1700s engines pumped water back over whee

CH01.name: Alchemy
CH01.fx: +1 Gold from Salt tiles in all cities — salt, one of the three principles.

CH04.name: Distillation
CH04.fx: Distillery [140/1; +2 Gold; Provides 1 Whisky <when number of [Worked Peat Cutting Tiles in this city] is more than 0>] — spirits, essential oils, perfume; and where the city cuts peat, whisky. Whisky — a new luxury resource (resourceType: Luxury; Doesn't generate naturally), made rather than mined, as Jewelry and Porcelain are: malted barley dried over peat smoke.
